name: Logfire
tagline: An open-source Python SDK for the Logfire observability platform, built on OpenTelemetry.
hook: An SDK and docs guide to realistic telemetry tests, source locations, CI coverage gates, and repository-backed checks.
summary: Logfire's CLAUDE.md covers the open-source SDK and docs, not the closed-source service. It calls for realistic telemetry tests, points documentation work to the right files, and checks CI or review findings against the repository's actual configuration.

techniques.title: Find the real enforcement point
techniques.body: Coverage has a 100% CI gate even though the local report configuration does not set a failure threshold. The guide names the workflow step to prevent a successful local command from being mistaken for proof.
techniques.quote: `[tool.coverage.report]` sets no `fail_under`, so reading `pyproject.toml` suggests there is no bar and a plain `coverage report` exits 0 on a regression.

techniques.title: Explain why matrix-wide coverage differs from local coverage
techniques.body: CI combines observations across test jobs, so a branch missed on one machine may be exercised elsewhere. The file prefers targeted local investigation and lets the combined CI result define complete coverage.
techniques.quote: CI combines coverage across the whole test matrix, so a line reached only by another matrix job looks missed on one machine, and a local number is both slow to get and misleading.

techniques.title: Preserve intentional warnings in production
techniques.body: Warnings-as-errors should be addressed in tests when the warning is deliberate. The file tells agents to expect or narrowly filter the warning instead of removing a useful user-facing signal.
techniques.quote: When a warning is intentional, update affected tests to expect it or narrow their warning filters instead of suppressing the warning in production code.

techniques.title: Verify a review finding against active rules
techniques.body: The review section gives a concrete example of a generally valid Ruff concern that does not apply because the rule is disabled here. It asks agents to inspect governing configuration before accepting or dismissing feedback.
techniques.quote: A reviewer can be right about Python in general and wrong about this repository.

techniques.title: Separate source-relative links from published routes
techniques.body: The docs workflow uses a navigation manifest to define public routes. It requires source-relative links and rendered preview checks, avoiding deployment prefixes that would be wrong in repository source.
techniques.quote:
Verify the page and any anchor in a rendered preview, and never include the
deployment-specific `/docs` prefix in source links.

steal: Point to the command that actually enforces a quality gate.
Explain when a combined CI metric cannot be reproduced on one machine.
Handle expected warnings in tests without hiding them in production.
Check review claims against enabled rules and local configuration.
Distinguish documentation source paths from published URLs.
